# CF-003: The proxy is not reachable on a public address while ingress is the tunnel

- **Group:** Cloudflare Tunnel
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

When the origin proxy also answers on a wildcard or public 80/443, anyone who finds the origin IP can bypass the tunnel and with it Cloudflare's WAF, Access policies and rate limits. Docker published ports skip UFW, so a 0.0.0.0:443 publish is open even under a default deny, unless the DOCKER-USER chain filters it: behind a standard ufw-docker chain it is open only when a ufw route rule allows the container port.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ss -tlnp | grep -E ':(80|443) '; from another machine: curl -kv https://<origin-ip>/
```

## How to fix it

Publish the proxy on 127.0.0.1 only (127.0.0.1:443:443) and let cloudflared reach it locally or over a Docker network

## What a fix can break

Anything that reached the origin directly (health checks, other CDNs, Let's Encrypt HTTP challenges) stops working; switch certificates to DNS challenges first.

Run `stackward explain CF-003` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
